excerpt: npm install @promptaudit/shieldimport { withShield } from "@promptaudit/shield"; const answer = await withShield(userPrompt, (safe) => llm.complete(safe)); // The model saw [API_KEY_1], [IBAN_1] … — your user gets the real values back.You wrote: Deploy with key sk-proj-AbC123…xyz and refund Mr. John Miller, IBAN CH93 0076 2011 6238 5295 7 Model sees: Deploy with key [API_KEY_1] and refund Mr. [NAME_1], IBAN [IBAN_1] You get: the model's answer with the original values restored in your process memory - Zero dependencies. One small TypeScript module. Browser, Node, Bun, Deno, edge workers. - Checksum-validated. IBAN (ISO 7064 Mod 97), cards (Luhn + brand prefix), US SSN (SSA rules), ABA routing (3-7-1). Order and serial numbers are not masked by accident. - Secrets included. OpenAI/Anthropic sk-…, AWS AKIA…/ASIA…, GitHub ghp_…/github_pat_…, Slack xox…-, JWT and PEM private keys. - Reversible. Placeholders go out, the map stays in your process memory. - Obfuscation-aware. Zero-width characters and full-width digits are normalised first. - No network, no telemetry. NLP stacks (e.g. Microsoft Presidio) detect free-text names and addresses, which Shield does not. Choose by need; they can be combined. IBAN · payment card · US SSN · US routing (with keyword) · e-mail · international phone (+ prefix) · names after Mr./Mrs./Ms./Dr./Prof. · API keys · private keys - Pattern-based, not NER: names without a title, free-text addresses and medical terms are not detected. - Unknown key formats are not caught. - Detection is best-effort. It reduces exposure; it does not guarantee that no personal data leaves your system. - No audit trail. Shield runs inside your code.
